standard_prerequisites.name: Wedderburn's theorem
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that every finite central simple algebra is a matrix algebra over a finite central skew field, which lets the author reduce to the third assertion.

standard_prerequisites.name: The endomorphism ring of a simple module
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that the endomorphism ring of a simple module over a matrix algebra is the opposite of the skew field, which distinguishes the skew fields up to isomorphism.

core_obligations: Reduction (proof lines 621-626): by Wedderburn's theorem every finite central simple algebra is a matrix algebra over a finite central skew field, so it suffices to prove the third assertion.

The third assertion (proof lines 627-630): if two matrix algebras over skew fields are isomorphic, then taking a simple module and using the identification of its endomorphism ring with the opposite of the skew field shows that the two skew fields have isomorphic opposites and hence are isomorphic; this also yields the uniqueness in the second assertion and the equivalence relation property.
proof_roadmap: Write every finite central simple algebra as a matrix algebra over a skew field.
Compare the endomorphism rings of simple modules to recover the skew field up to isomorphism.
Read off the equivalence relation and the uniqueness of the skew field in a similarity class.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that similarity of finite central simple algebras is an equivalence relation, that every class contains a unique finite central skew field, and that two matrix algebras over skew fields are similar exactly when the skew fields are isomorphic (statement lines 607-619). The proof is a complete argument: Wedderburn's theorem writes every such algebra as a matrix algebra over a skew field, reducing the statement to the third assertion (proof lines 621-626); and there the endomorphism ring of a simple module is identified with the opposite of the skew field, so an isomorphism of the matrix algebras forces the skew fields to be isomorphic (proof lines 627-630). The non-formal content is the reduction and the use of the endomorphism ring as an invariant. The claim is H2.
